paper.title_en: Design and characterization of neutron time-of-flight detector prototypes for heavy-ion collision experiments at CEE
paper.abstract_en: The CSR External-Target Experiment (CEE) at the Heavy Ion Research Facility in Lanzhou (HIRFL) will provide unique experimental opportunities for studying high-density nuclear matter, for which high-precision neutron measurements are essential to constrain the symmetry energy and the nuclear equation of state. Prototype modules of a multi-layer sampling neutron time-of-flight (TOF) detector, each consisting of three EJ-200 plastic scintillator layers and three lead absorber layers arranged alternately and read out by silicon photomultipliers (SiPMs), have been developed and characterized. Geant4 simulations showed that the detection efficiency increases with the absorber thickness, and that cascading more than 25 modules can push the efficiency above 90%. The SiPM readout circuit and the series-parallel interconnection scheme were optimized, and the 6-series-2-parallel (6S2P) configuration was adopted. Cosmic ray muon tests at an operating voltage of 195 V demonstrated intrinsic time resolutions of 45, 85, and 112 ps for the modules with 4, 6, and 8 mm absorbers, respectively. After including the neutron interaction-position uncertainty, the estimated neutron TOF resolutions for these modules are 70, 105, and 132 ps, respectively, all better than 150 ps, satisfying the requirements of next-generation neutron TOF measurements.
